subject: MAP, legal sequencing & target close plan — Nexa Health pilot
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Procurement (Nexa Health) <procurement@nexahealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: MAP, legal sequencing & target close plan — Nexa Health pilot

Hi team,

Thanks again for the productive demo last week. As discussed, I pulled together a short mutual action plan (attached) that maps evaluation milestones to the legal/procurement steps we expect for a pilot-to-paid conversion. Our working target from the product side is to have Licenses + MSA/DPA + PO in place by 15 Dec — this aligns with your stated Q4 budget window.

Key asks from Redwood to Nexa Health:
- Confirm the internal approvers and their target sign dates (we added suggested names in the MAP).
- Tell us whether your procurement requires a vendor security package prior to legal redlines (SOC2 + data flow diagram are ready).
- If you expect any non-standard MSA terms, flag them now so we can parallelize legal review.

Attached: Redwood_MAP_v2.xlsx (roadmap + owner matrix), Redwood_MSA_draft_v3.docx (working draft).

Next steps: If procurement can confirm approvers by end of week we’ll propose a detailed close cadence (kanban-style milestones + handoff events). Jordan will coordinate the pilot SSO/infra checklist once we lock the PO timing.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

Attachments: Redwood_MAP_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), Redwood_MSA_draft_v3.docx (word doc)

From: Procurement (Nexa Health) <procurement@nexahealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: N. Patel <npatel@nexahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2027 12:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP, legal sequencing & target close plan — Nexa Health pilot

Marissa,

Appreciate the MAP. High level this looks reasonable — the 15 Dec target is our preference. A couple of procurement constraints to call out:
- Our legal team requires an executed DPA before any pilot data is ingested. We typically push for limited retention and a restriction on upstream model training; please confirm those clauses are present or acceptable.
- Purchase orders must reference an approved MSA version; we can accept DocuSign signature routing, but our internal sign-off (CFO + Procurement Dir) needs an MSA clean copy at least 7 business days before final signature.

Can you confirm: do you have a final DPA available or would Redwood prefer to work off our DPA? Also please provide SOC2 report and a concise data flow diagram (redlines will follow).

Thanks,
Procurement Team
Nexa Health

--
Procurement (Nexa Health)
procurement@nexahealth.com
Attachments: procurement_requirements.pdf (procurement checklist)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP, legal sequencing & target close plan — Nexa Health pilot

Thanks — confirmed. We can meet your DPA-before-ingest requirement. Laura (copied) will lead DPA redlines; we’ll propose limited retention language and the training restriction language you referenced.

To make progress in parallel, I’ve attached an updated MAP that includes:
- Milestone A (pilot activation): DPA executed + PO received + infra checklist done — target 2027-11-29
- Milestone B (pilot evaluation): 2-week test window + success metrics review — target 2027-12-08
- Milestone C (conversion): Final MSA signature + PO for production — target 2027-12-15

Owners:
- Redwood legal: Laura Bennett (redlines + DPA)
- Redwood ops: Jordan Blake (infra/SSO)
- Nexa procurement: Procurement Team (contract approval + PO)

Jordan — can you confirm the list of infra artifacts you’ll need from Nexa to schedule the pilot window?

Laura — I’ll send the MSA + DPA and ask for a 48-hour initial read; if you see any high-impact items we’ll raise ASAP.

Marissa

Attachments: Redwood_MAP_v2.xlsx (updated tab: milestone dates)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Procurement (Nexa Health) <procurement@nexahealth.com>
Cc: M. Murphy <mmurphy@bakerreed.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2027 10:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP, legal sequencing & target close plan — Nexa Health pilot

Marissa / Nexa procurement — I reviewed the MSA and DPA drafts and have a few flags that will affect sequencing if we need to negotiate them:

1) Data retention and training restriction: Redwood can accept a limited retention window but requests a clear definition of permitted uses (pilot debugging vs model training). If Nexa requires a hard prohibition on any training-use, that will change our outbound data handling and may require a scoped addendum.

2) Subprocessors / Flow-downs: We need a definitive list of third-party subprocessors you expect us to accept or a SOC2 + subprocessor attestation. We can provide the attestation quickly but if Nexa requires named approval for each subprocessor the review will add 5–7 business days.

3) Indemnity caps & liability carve-outs: The current MSA draft includes Redwood standard language; Nexa’s procurement_requirements.pdf suggests alternate cap language. Please confirm whether Nexa needs those alternate caps for CFO approval.

If Nexa can confirm: (a) training-use restriction level (none / limited / none-with-addendum), (b) whether subprocessors can be approved via attestation, and (c) desired liability cap, we can update the MAP timeline accordingly. I’m copying our outside counsel (M. Murphy) for any complex redline discussion.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Cc: N. Patel <npatel@nexahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Nov 2027 16:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP, legal sequencing & target close plan — Nexa Health pilot

Laura / Marissa,

Appreciate the quick review. Quick answers to your bullets:
- Training-use restriction: Nexa requests a limited-training prohibition for pilot data (no model training on identifiable pilot data). Limited retention is acceptable; we’ll accept your proposed retention window if it’s documented in the DPA.
- Subprocessors: Attestation acceptable for all standard cloud infra (we do require named approval for any analytics or third-party model tuning providers).
- Liability caps: CFO prefers a moderate cap (3x fees) — we can confirm final number with finance, but that is Nexa’s starting position.

We’re aligned on the 15 Dec signature target. For PO routing: please confirm whether Redwood prefers a single-signature DocuSign flow or a two-step (legal sign then CFO sign) that we can mirror in our PO. If you send the MSA clean copy to finance by 6 Dec we can meet the 15 Dec target.

Next steps we propose:
- 4 Nov: Procurement confirms subprocessors policy (this email)
- 5 Nov: Redwood to provide DPA updated draft reflecting limited-training prohibition
- 9 Nov: Nexa legal returns any material redlines to Redwood
- 29 Nov: Pilot activation (DPA + infra checklist + PO)
- 15 Dec: Final MSA + PO signature

CFO N. Patel is cc’d for awareness. We’ll escalate if legal needs further details from outside counsel.

Best,
Procurement Team
Nexa Health
